web_blocks.html: Donnelley Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: DFIN) closed at $64.53 on November 20, 2026 ($1.57 billion market cap; $1.68 billion EV) [30]. Spun off from R.R. Donnelley in October 2016, DFIN grew Software Solutions to 51.5% of Q3 2026 sales ($95.2 million of $185.0 million) [3, 45, 46]. Nine-month free cash flow reached $131.0 million, net debt fell to $99.8 million (0.4x TTM Adjusted EBITDA of $253.1 million), and ROIC stands at 18.25% [30, 45, 46]. However, Pass 1 downgraded KPI health to PASS_WITH_WATCH under a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict. IC-SS (Arc Suite) fell -1.9% YoY in Q3, and CM-SS Adjusted EBITDA dropped -6.8% YoY (-490 bps to 30.0%) [45]. Five officers sold 201,650 shares in early November (mostly non-10b5-1) alongside GCM President Craig Clay's departure [47, 48]. Meanwhile, Workiva spent $167.7 million on 9M R&D (4.5x DFIN's CapEx), and SEC 2026 rulemaking threatens $109.4 million in Print & Distribution [53, 56].

Re-underwriting valuation cleanly lowers our 12–18 month SOTP Base Fair Value from $92.00 to $74.00 (near the $75.33 Finviz consensus) [30]. Bull and Bear targets stand at $88.00 and $50.00, giving a $70.80 probability-weighted expected value. Despite a Stage 2 tag, shares sit +15.65% above the 50-day SMA ($55.80) with a falling 4-hour RSI (42.89, no turn) inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend (38.8% >50-DMA) [30]. Options are also illiquid (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID). Against the $47.46 stop, reward-to-risk to $74.00 is 0.55:1 at $64.53 CMP, 0.49:1 at $65.27 support top, and 1.49:1 at $58.12 support bottom. Every level inside the snapshot band fails 1.50:1. We assign REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, TREND, BUSINESS), hold 0 shares (NOT_HELD), and keep 100% of capital in USD Cash.

web_blocks.title: Re-Review Gate (What Must Change Before DFIN Can Leave REJECTED Status)
paragraphs: 1. Segment & Margin Cure: CM-SS Adjusted EBITDA margin rebounds above 33% and Arc Suite (IC-SS) returns to positive organic growth [45].
2. Governance & Dilution Cure: Share buybacks exceed $8.5M/quarter SBC and senior executives halt discretionary non-10b5-1 sales [45, 48].
3. Valuation & Macro Reset: Price resets toward $53.21–$55.80 (or fair value rises above $85) inside a Confirmed Uptrend rather than a 10-distribution-day Downtrend [30].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to Chapter Zero—the executive briefing for our refreshed ten-chapter institutional monograph on Donnelley Financial Solutions, ticker DFIN, as of the November 20, 2026 market close at $64.53 per share.

If you remember one lesson from this refresh, make it this: unbiased investing means updating your verdict when new evidence weakens the thesis, never clinging to yesterday's $92 target. On November 16, DFIN looked like an extended software transformation waiting for a pullback. Four days later, after stripping away prior targets and running a fresh forensic audit on Q3 filings, Form 4 insider sales, competitor spending, and the November 20 tape, the conclusion flips decisively to REJECTED.

To be clear, DFIN is not a broken business. Nine-month operating cash flow jumped 59% to $167.3 million, free cash flow hit $131.0 million, net debt dropped to $99.8 million, Software Solutions crossed 51.5% of Q3 revenue, and ROIC sits at 18.25%. Yet Pass 1 uncovered six serious watch flags that reshape the investment math. Arc Suite stalled at -1.9% in Q3. Capital Markets Software lost 490 basis points of margin as SG&A surged 22.4%. Workiva turned GAAP profitable while outspending DFIN 4.5-to-1 on R&D, and the SEC's 2026 agenda threatens Form N-PORT and $109.4 million of Print and Distribution revenue. Meanwhile, five senior executives dumped 201,650 shares in early November—mostly outside 10b5-1 plans—while Q3 buybacks fell below quarterly stock compensation.

Resetting our Sum-of-the-Parts valuation to reflect those facts lowers Base Fair Value from $92.00 to $74.00—aligned with the $75.33 Wall Street consensus. At $64.53 today, against a $47.46 structural stop, reward-to-risk is just 0.55-to-1. Even at the $58.12 floor of the snapshot support band, reward-to-risk reaches only 1.49-to-1—still failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle—while shares remain 15.65% extended above the 50-day SMA inside a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend.

Therefore, our verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0) based on VALUATION, TREND, and BUSINESS headwinds. DFIN is NOT_HELD across our accounts, and we keep 100% of earmarked capital safe in USD Cash—passing for now on shortlist peer AvePoint and outside peer Brown & Brown—until either DFIN cures its margin and insider-selling watch flags at a deeper price reset, or broader market breadth recovers.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Zero Allegiance to Yesterday's Target
book_callouts.text: The whole point of a two-pass companion refresh is preventing confirmation bias. When Pass 1 uncovers margin compression, 201,650 shares of executive selling, and a 4.5x R&D gap at Workiva, Pass 2 refuses to defend a stale $92 target—resetting fair value to $74 and assigning REJECTED.

book_subsections.title: 0A. Five Anchor Numbers for This November 20 Refresh
paragraphs: Keep five numbers top of mind as you listen. First, $64.53: the November 20 close, down 10.4% from the $72.04 peak yet still 15.65% above the 50-day SMA ($55.80). Second, 201,650 shares: the November 2–13 executive selling wave, mostly outside automatic 10b5-1 plans.

Third, -490 basis points: the Q3 margin compression in Capital Markets Software, leaving legacy print-assisted CCM earning higher quarterly EBITDA. Fourth, $74.00: our re-underwritten Base Fair Value, aligning with $75.33 consensus. Fifth, 0.55-to-1: current reward-to-risk against the $47.46 structural stop, failing our 1.50-to-1 gate.

book_subsections.title: 0B. How the Blind Two-Pass Audit Protected Capital
paragraphs: Without stripping out prior prices and targets in Pass 1, it is all too easy to rationalize Q3 watch flags and keep waiting passively at $64.55. By auditing the footnotes, Form 4 filings, and Workiva's R&D gap cold, then re-computing valuation from scratch in Pass 2, the math spoke clearly: $74.00 fair value cannot justify buying an extended small-cap in a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend.

That two-stage firewall is what separates disciplined underwriting from confirmation bias. Pass 1 read only primary SEC filings, Form 4 insider tables, and competitor disclosures—never once peeking at the prior $92 target. When Pass 2 finally opened the live November 20 tape, the facts spoke for themselves.

book_subsections.title: 0C. Why Cash Beats Chasing Inside a 10-Distribution-Day Downtrend
paragraphs: Remember the market backdrop on November 20, 2026. Only 38.8% of tracked US stocks trade above their 50-day moving averages, only three of eleven sectors hold intermediate uptrends, and the S&P 500 has printed 10 institutional distribution days in 25 sessions while 10-year Treasury yields sit at 5.04%.

In that environment, paying +15.65% above the 50-day SMA for a small-cap hybrid whose top five executives just sold 0.82% of the company—and whose options chain has >14% spreads—offers poor odds. Keeping 100% of capital in USD Cash protects principal until breadth recovers and DFIN either resets to $53.21–$55.80 with cured margins or gives way to cleaner leaders.

book_subsections.title: 0D. What You Will Hear Across Chapters 1 Through 9
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 trace DFIN's ten-year evolution from its October 2016 R.R. Donnelley spin-off through its four-segment operating grid, FY2025 cash conversion waterfall, Workiva and VDR competitive landscape, management's governance and Form 4 audit, and balance-sheet footnote forensics.

Chapters 7 through 9 then open the live November 20 valuation and Stage 2 tape—walking step-by-step through the Reverse DCF, the $74.00 SOTP reset, the 1W/1D/4H technical deterioration, and our final REJECTED action plan.

book_subsections.title: 0E. Why This Refresh Overrides the Prior November 16 Verdict
paragraphs: Listeners comparing this November 20 edition against the earlier November 16 monograph will notice a decisive shift: the prior edition carried a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT verdict with a $92.00 Base Target, whereas today's edition downgrades DFIN to REJECTED (TIER_0) with a $74.00 Base Target. That change was not driven by a four-day price wiggle from $70.06 to $64.53—it was driven by new forensic evidence.

Uncovering the November 2–13 executive Form 4 selling wave, May 2026 Global Capital Markets leadership departure, -490 bps CM-SS margin compression, flat Arc Suite organic growth, $167.7 million Workiva R&D spend, and SEC e-delivery default proposals fundamentally lowered the fair value we can defend with integrity. When the valuation ceiling drops from $92.00 to $74.00, the math across the entire $58.12–$65.27 support band fails 1.50-to-1, and anti-hedging rules compel an honest REJECTED verdict.

book_subsections.title: 0F. Summary of Capital Action and Opportunity Cost
paragraphs: Before we dive into Chapter 1, lock in the exact portfolio action as of November 20, 2026. DFIN is NOT_HELD across both Charles Schwab and Robinhood, with zero shares and zero open options. Because options spreads exceed 14% and reward-to-risk sits at 0.55-to-1 at $64.53 (and 0.49-to-1 to 1.49-to-1 across the snapshot support band), zero new capital is authorized.

Instead, 100% of earmarked tactical funds remain safely in USD Cash earning risk-free Treasury yield while the S&P 500 digests 10 distribution days on 38.8% breadth—explicitly benchmarked against active shortlist leader AvePoint (AVPT, 0% allocation in Downtrend) and outside Stage 2 peer Brown & Brown (BRO, 0% allocation).

book_subsections.title: 0G. Reading Roadmap for the Complete Ten-Chapter Audit
paragraphs: As you listen through this monograph, pay special attention to the blind-spot patches in Chapters 2 through 6—covering SEC e-delivery risks, CM-SS margin compression, Workiva's $167.7 million R&D spend, the 201,650-share November insider selling wave, and balance-sheet goodwill forensics. Those primary SEC disclosures explain why Pass 2 cleanly reset Base Fair Value to $74.00 and rejected new capital.

Whether you read the full web monograph with interactive charts and data tables or listen to the narrative edition end to end, every number reconciles back to audited SEC filings and the verified November 20, 2026 market close.

Just as importantly, keep our portfolio discipline front and center across all ten chapters. Protecting cash in a ten-distribution-day market Downtrend is how you keep capital ready for asymmetric Stage 2 leaders when breadth recovers. Let's begin Chapter 1 now.
